title: Flux Cup
description: A reimagined disposable polymer cup designed to improve usability and sustainability.
overview: Flux Cup is a redesign exercise focused on improving ergonomics, spill resistance, and material efficiency of disposable polymer cups.
outcome: Presented a refined product concept, design calculations, CAD model, and renderings.
highlights: Created CAD drawings and realistic renderings using Fusion 360, Blender, and Blender fluid simulation.
Evaluated stacking stress during design for easy storage.

title: Swarm Sense
description: Using rainfall measurements and field data to identify likely mosquito breeding grounds.
overview: Swarm Sense explored how environmental datasets can help cover gaps in mosquito-breeding risk identification and mitigation.
outcome: We won the Intermediate Division of the NASA GeoEMERGE Challenge by creating an integrated Folium map of historic rainfall trends and field data to determine mosquito breeding grounds.
highlights: Presented a complete concept with supporting research and visuals to 5 rotating panels of judges.
Worked in under 2 hours to create a defined project from an open-ended public health question.
Wrangled large datasets using Pandas and Matplotlib to create visualizations for an interactive map.

title: Canvas Pets
description: A Chrome extension that turns assignment completion into a motivating experience for K–8 students.
overview: Canvas Pets is a Canvas-integrated Chrome extension that makes school progress visible and playful, encouraging students to build momentum through small rewards.
role: Hackathon Team Member, Product Concept Development, Visual Design (Pixel Art)
outcome: Built a working Chrome-extension concept during SwampHacks XI, with a playful visual system and student-centered motivation loop.
highlights: Created custom pixel-art companions, extension wallpaper, and animated interface assets in Aseprite.
Developed concept plans and roadmap for hackathon development strategy.

title: Medlog
description: A medical-transcription and sharing platform built during my first hackathon.
overview: Medlog is a concept for reducing the friction of recording, organizing, and sharing medical information across appointments and care teams.
role: Hackathon Team Member, AI Integration (Clinical Transcriptions), Technical Write-Up
outcome: Produced a cohesive platform concept and presentation during the DTE Designathon 2025. This challenge was also my first hackathon experience!
highlights: Scoped a compliant solution for a sensitive, real-world information-management problem.
Developed a clear product narrative with industry insights for final presentation.
Integrated GeminiAPI into python software to enhance clinical transcription accuracy and summary generation speed.

title: Carbon Fiber Product Development Intern
description: Conducted research and development on carbon fiber composites.
overview: Explored conductive, thermal, and mechanical properties of various composite materials to inform industrial product development.
role: R&D Intern, Product Characterization, Composite Manufacturing
outcome: Presented research findings and recommendations for future development to sales and senior engineering teams. I also met plenty of amazing people and truly enjoyed my three months at Zoltek!
highlights: Closed 3 research studies on composite conductivity thresholds for sales data using DOE for various percolation studies in accordance with ASTM, ISO, and IEC standards.
Accelerated the fiber sizing verification process by engineering a multi-flask DCM reflux system, reducing processing time by 75% and doubling batch capacity.
Characterized composite thermal and compositional properties using Ultrasonic NDT, Instron Mechanical tests, DMA, TGA, FTIR, and DSC.
Optimized catalyst and resin formulations via gel curve analysis, viscosity testing, and stability studies to improve pilot-scale production.

title: Radome Analysis for Wildfire Response UAVs
description: Analyzed potential nosecone/radome configurations for UAVs used in wildfire response.
overview: This project aimed to conceptually design and analyze composite UAV radome materials to enhance performance during wildfire reconnaissance.
outcome: I presented a technical write-up of my analysis and recommendations of materials-first solutions to improve UAV survival in wildfire response scenarios, scoring a 97/100.
highlights: Developed merit-based material selection criteria for UAV radome applications, considering factors such as thermal resistance, mechanical strength, and electromagnetic transparency.
Modeled and rendered blunted-ogive radome configurations using Fusion360
Recommended molding 30% Glass-Fiber PEEK for optimal performance, achieving a 100°C increase over previous thermal limits in PU radome core.

title: IREC Composites Engineer
description: Manufacturing student-designed rocket components for the International Rocketry Challenge (IREC).
overview: Precision manufacturing of composite rocket components for participation in the annual International Rocketry Challenge (IREC).
role: IREC Manufacturing, Launch Safety Analysis, Technical Documentation
outcome: Successfully contributed to the development of 10+ composite rocket components per IREC competition cycle.
highlights: Fabricated couplers, airframes, and nosecones for high-performance rockets comprising 80% of the total structure.
Optimized layup process time by 50% by controlling epoxy formulation, vacuum cure, and post processsing.
Reduced competition fin thickness by 48% while maintaining structural integrity using team-first tip-to-tip layups and prepreg/autoclave sandwich panel cures.

title: Composites Development Engineer
description: Advancing Swamp Launch's composite fabrication capabilities under the Spaceshot Development Program.
overview: With the development division, I develope the next generation of innovative composite solutions for Swamp Launch's SRAD rocket applications.
outcome: Began development of advanced composite fabrication techniques and material analysis to support 100,000 ft. rocket launch.
highlights: Designed and operated preliminary tests of student-designed filament winder. Adopted open-source 'Cyclone' winding software to optimize winding patterns for composite rocket components.
(In Progress) Development of Filament Winder V2.0, improving eyelet placement, mandrel stability, and stepper-motor torque to handle consistent composite layups.
(In-Progress) Development of lap-shear protocol and analysis for testing of prepreg-foam sandwiches.

title: HAB Payload Engineer
description: 14 students across Florida designed 3 High Altitude Balloon payloads for near-space research.
overview: As an engineer and media liaison for FSGC, I worked on integrating the payloads and coordinating with the media team.
role: Media Liaison, Payload Integration, Thermal Simulation and Analysis
outcome: Gained valuable knowledge in cross-disciplinary and remote collaboration. Created a media package for FSGC and Space Trek Academy to promote the project and its results.
highlights: Developed a payload to analyze convective heat transfer collapse in Aluminum components with altitude. Simulated thermal performance outcomes using custom python scripts and Solidworks Thermal Analysis.
Managed $700 budget and 8lb weight limit to successfully integrate 3/3 student payloads.
Created a 5 minute documentary highlighting the project and its results featuring student interviews and footage. Amassed over 120 clean photos to be used in the media package.

title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
description: Analyzing open source thermodynamics software "PyCALPHAD" for the MONSTER research group.
overview: The MONSTER research group focuses on the development and application of inorganic materials science. My research focuses on thermodynamics and phase transformations.
outcome: Gained experience in thermodynamics, phase transformations, and materials science research.
highlights: (In Progress) Analyzing the potential transition to opensource thermodynamics software "PyCALPHAD" for the MONSTER research group.
(In Progress) Gaining experience in thermodynamics, phase transformations, and materials science research.
